overview.title: Project Architecture
overview.purpose: A source-backed map of the major responsibilities and contracts.
overview.summary: Use this overview to orient around entrypoints, runtime work, state, delivery, and signal.
overview.why: It gives maintainers a first map before they dive into files.
points: Select a node to inspect its contracts.
Use focus modes to narrow the reading path.
Source confidence labels should remain visible in chips.

runtime.title: Runtime Flow
runtime.purpose: Request handling through core workflow and user-visible result.
runtime.summary: Highlights the direct path from user entry to durable state and reporting.
runtime.why: Most debugging starts by finding where the runtime contract broke.
points: Router and policy decide whether work can start.
Workflow engine owns the core transition.
State and reporting define externally visible results.

delivery.title: Delivery Flow
delivery.purpose: How project changes become runnable behavior.
delivery.summary: Connects CI/release gates to runtime deployment and operational evidence.
delivery.why: Build and release systems often explain production behavior drift.
points: Validate delivery contracts before blaming runtime.
Release signals should point back to runtime versions.

debugging.title: Debugging Flow
debugging.purpose: The first places to inspect when the system breaks.
debugging.summary: Focuses on runtime, async work, release status, and observability evidence.
debugging.why: Useful architecture docs shorten incident orientation time.
points: Separate delivery failure from runtime failure.
Check async queues when direct requests succeeded but side effects did not.
